sections.title: Pair of Straight Lines
sections.content: A homogeneous equation ax²+2hxy+by²=0 represents two lines passing through the origin. Angle θ between them: tanθ = 2√(h²-ab) / |a+b|. Lines are perpendicular if a+b=0, coincident if h²=ab.

sections.title: Angle Bisectors of Two Lines
sections.content: For lines L1=0 and L2=0, bisectors are (a1x+b1y+c1)/√(a1²+b1²) = ±(a2x+b2y+c2)/√(a2²+b2²). The sign (+ or -) distinguishes between the acute and obtuse angle bisectors based on the sign of a1a2+b1b2.

sections.title: Family of Circles
sections.content: 1) Through intersection of 2 circles: S1 + λS2 = 0. 2) Through intersection of circle and line: S + λL = 0. 3) Through two given points (x1,y1) & (x2,y2): Use diametric form + λ(Line through points) = 0.

sections.title: Common Tangents to Two Circles
sections.content: Count depends on distance between centers (d) and radii (r1, r2). d > r1+r2 (4 tangents). d = r1+r2 (3 tangents). |r1-r2| < d < r1+r2 (2 tangents). d = |r1-r2| (1 tangent). d < |r1-r2| (0 tangents).

sections.title: Orthogonal Circles
sections.content: Two circles intersect at 90° (orthogonally) if the tangents at the intersection point are perpendicular. Condition: 2g1g2 + 2f1f2 = c1 + c2.

sections.title: Radical Axis and Radical Center
sections.content: Radical axis is the locus of a point with equal tangent lengths to two circles: S1 - S2 = 0 (ensure x², y² coefficients are 1). Radical center is the intersection of radical axes of 3 circles.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Writing S1 - S2 = 0 for radical axis without making the coefficients of x² and y² equal to 1 first.
2) Using the wrong sign when determining acute/obtuse angle bisectors without making c1, c2 positive first.
3) Confusing transverse common tangents (intersect line joining centers) with direct common tangents.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 targets complex JEE Advanced loci, joint equations (homogenization), systems of circles (radical axis/orthogonal), and identifying exact bisectors/tangents algebraically.

tricks.title: Acute/Obtuse Bisector Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Make constants c1, c2 positive. Calculate 'a1a2 + b1b2'. If >0, the '+' sign gives the obtuse bisector. If <0, the '+' sign gives the acute bisector.
tricks.example: Check sign of a1a2+b1b2, then match (+ with obtuse if >0, + with acute if <0).

tricks.title: Perpendicular Pair of Lines
tricks.explanation: In any 2nd-degree equation ax²+2hxy+by²+2gx+2fy+c=0, the lines are perpendicular if the sum of coefficients of x² and y² is zero.

tricks.title: Length of Common Tangents
tricks.explanation: Direct Common Tangent (DCT) = √[d² - (r1-r2)²]. Transverse Common Tangent (TCT) = √[d² - (r1+r2)²].

tricks.title: Homogenization (Curve & Line Intersection)
tricks.explanation: To find the joint equation of lines joining the origin to intersection points of a curve and a line Lx+My=1, multiply linear terms of the curve by (Lx+My) and constant by (Lx+My)².
tricks.example: Curve x²+y²+2x=0, Line x+y=1. Joint eq: x²+y²+2x(x+y) = 0 → 3x²+y²+2xy=0.

tricks.title: Centers of Similitude for Tangents
tricks.explanation: Direct common tangents pass through the external center of similitude (divides centers externally in r1:r2). TCTs pass through the internal center of similitude.
tricks.example: Use external section formula for ratio r1:r2 to find the point where DCTs intersect.

tricks.title: Radical Axis Orthogonal Trick
tricks.explanation: The radical axis of two circles is ALWAYS perpendicular to the line joining their centers.
tricks.example: If centers are on the X-axis (y=0), the radical axis is a vertical line (x=k).
